title: Given a Scenario, Implement Best Practices Associated with Documentation and Support Systems Information Management

sections.title: What You Are Learning
paragraphs: Strong technical work must be supported by records that identify the user and device, describe and prioritize the issue, preserve troubleshooting history, document the resolution, track organizational assets, and share repeatable procedures and solutions.
sections.callout: Track the issue → track the asset → document the process → share the knowledge.

sections.title: Maestro Focus
paragraphs: Match each support scenario to the proper record: ticket, asset record, configuration management database, incident report, standard operating procedure, checklist, service-level agreement, or knowledge-base article.

sections.title: Ticketing Systems
paragraphs: A ticketing system tracks one support request from creation through resolution so technicians know what happened, who is affected, what has been tried, and what remains.
sections.callout: One problem → one tracked support record.

entries.title: User Information
paragraphs: Record the user's name, department, contact information, and relevant location so the affected person can be identified and reached.

entries.title: Device Information
paragraphs: Identify the exact device with details such as computer name, asset tag, serial number, model, and operating system.

entries.title: Description of Issues
paragraphs: Explain what happens, when it began, what should happen, any error shown, and whether the symptom is repeatable. Record facts instead of vague statements or assumptions.

entries.title: Categories
paragraphs: Classify tickets as hardware, software, network, account, printer, or another approved category for routing, reporting, prioritization, and trend analysis.

sections.title: Severity and Escalation Levels

entries.title: Severity
paragraphs: Severity reflects technical and business impact, including users affected, system criticality, outage scope, and available workarounds.

entries.title: Escalation Levels
paragraphs: Escalation transfers the ticket to a person or team with the permissions, expertise, authority, or responsibility needed to continue.

sections.callout: Impact → severity; next support level → escalation.

sections.title: Clear, Concise Written Communication
paragraphs: Ticket notes must allow another technician to continue the work without guessing.

entries.title: Issue Description
paragraphs: Document the initial symptom with useful facts and scope.

entries.title: Progress Notes
paragraphs: Record steps performed, results, changes, tests, and user communication during troubleshooting.

entries.title: Issue Resolution
paragraphs: State the root cause when known, the final corrective action, and how successful operation was verified.

sections.callout: During troubleshooting → progress notes; completed fix → issue resolution.

sections.title: Asset Management
paragraphs: Asset management tracks organizational hardware, software, ownership, assignment, status, coverage, and life-cycle information.
sections.callout: What do we own, where is it, and who has it?

sections.title: Inventory Lists and Configuration Management Database (CMDB)

entries.title: Inventory Lists
paragraphs: An inventory list records assets such as device, model, serial number, location, and current status.

entries.title: Configuration Management Database (CMDB)
paragraphs: A CMDB records configuration items, their settings, and relationships or dependencies among servers, workstations, applications, and network devices.

sections.callout: What assets exist → inventory; how assets are configured and related → CMDB.

sections.title: Asset Tags and IDs
paragraphs: A unique asset tag identifies one exact company device and connects it to ownership, assignment, service history, warranty, and replacement records.
sections.callout: This exact device → asset tag or ID.

sections.title: Procurement Life Cycle
paragraphs: The procurement life cycle follows an asset from request and purchase through receipt, deployment, maintenance, and retirement.
sections.callout: Request → purchase → receive → deploy → maintain → retire.

sections.title: Warranty and Licensing
paragraphs: Asset records may track hardware warranty expiration, software licenses, subscriptions, renewal dates, and license assignments.
sections.callout: Are we covered, supported, and legally licensed?

sections.title: Assigned Users
paragraphs: Asset management should identify the person responsible for or currently assigned to each device.

sections.title: Types of Documents
paragraphs: Select a document based on its purpose: formal event record, repeatable process, employee checklist, service commitment, or reusable technical guidance.

sections.title: Incident Reports
paragraphs: An incident report formally documents a significant security event, hardware-damage event, outage, or policy violation. An incident may also have related support tickets, but the records serve different purposes.

sections.title: Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs)
paragraphs: An SOP defines an approved repeatable process that improves consistency, training, quality, compliance, and safety.

entries.title: Software Package Custom Installation Procedure
paragraphs: Document the organization's approved installation source, required options, licensing, configuration, and verification steps for custom software deployment.

sections.callout: Perform the task the same approved way every time.

sections.title: Onboarding and Off-Boarding Checklists

entries.title: New User/Onboarding Setup Checklist
paragraphs: Ensure a new employee receives the required account, computer, email, group memberships, applications, permissions, and MFA enrollment.

entries.title: User Off-Boarding Checklist
paragraphs: Disable accounts, recover equipment, remove access, revoke tokens, transfer data, and reclaim licenses when a user leaves.

sections.callout: Join → provide authorized access and assets; leave → revoke access and recover assets.

sections.title: Service-Level Agreements (SLAs)
paragraphs: An SLA defines expected response time, resolution targets, availability, and responsibilities.

entries.title: Internal
paragraphs: An internal SLA establishes expectations between teams or departments inside one organization.

entries.title: External/Third-Party
paragraphs: An external or third-party SLA establishes service commitments between the organization and an ISP, cloud vendor, managed service provider, or other supplier.

sections.callout: Team to team → internal SLA; company to vendor → external SLA.

sections.title: Knowledge Base and Articles
paragraphs: A knowledge base stores reusable fixes, troubleshooting steps, FAQs, and configuration instructions for future cases.
sections.callout: One user's case → ticket; reusable answer for many cases → knowledge-base article.

table.caption: Choose the record that matches the need

sections.title: Recognition Cues
bullets: Who reported the problem → user information
Which device is affected → device information
Transfer to the proper support level → escalation
Final fix and verification → issue resolution
List of company assets → inventory list
Purchase through retirement → procurement life cycle
Coverage and usage rights → warranty and licensing
Who has the device → assigned user

sections.title: Objective 4.1 Exam Trap
bullets: Severity measures impact; escalation identifies the support level that must handle the issue.
A ticket records support work; an incident report formally documents a significant event.
Inventory says what assets exist; a CMDB also records configuration and relationships.
An SOP defines an approved process; a knowledge-base article preserves reusable troubleshooting guidance.
Onboarding grants approved access and resources; off-boarding removes access and recovers assets.
An internal SLA applies between organizational groups; an external SLA applies between the organization and a third party.

sections.title: Maestro Recognition Sheet
bullets: Purchase through disposal → procurement life cycle
Hardware or software coverage → warranty and licensing
sections.callout: Track the issue → track the asset → document the process → share the knowledge.
